rationale: Three numerical-passing, compiling observations: attempt-00 (128x64x64, stages=1, swizzle=0) 470.78 us; attempt-01 (64x128x64, stages=1, swizzle=16) 402.23 us; attempt-02 (64x128x32, stages=2, swizzle=16) 399.54 us. All hit 32768 actual smem exactly at the portability cap, and simulated_dram_mb is identical (16.78) across runs, so the simulator does not show swizzle-driven DRAM savings — the analytical panel-reuse traffic term is not materializing as measured traffic. The only latency gain from attempt-01 to attempt-02 came from halving block_K and doubling stages (traffic down, pipeline deeper), not from swizzle, though swizzle=16 was present in both best runs. Keep swizzle [0,4,8,16] to test whether swizzle>0 helps at matched tile/stage and to disambiguate the confounded evidence; keep all tile/stage domains full so HiGHS can trade tile size for extra stages under the 32KB cap (multi-stage at 64x128x32 fits; larger tiles at stages>1 are pruned by the bound). Adjust weights: raise pipeline to 2 because deeper staging at smaller block_K is the clearest observed lever (attempt-02 best) and stages have been pinned at 1-2 by smem; lower footprint to 0.5 since actual smem sits exactly at the hard cap in every run, so the constraint already enforces footprint pressure and extra weighting only distorts the ranking. Traffic stays 1 since measured DRAM is flat and the analytical term is unreliable; launches stays 1 to avoid overfitting three points. Next hypothesis: at matched tile (64x128x32) compare swizzle=0 vs 16 to see if locality is real; also probe stages=3 with block_K=32 and block_M=32 to test whether deeper pipelining lowers simulated latency further. Validation scope: Metal checks execute the exact source/config/TIR, but CUDA binaries are not executed on GB10; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. No global optimality is claimed.
